items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Would you say that the rhythm section, that was Baby Dodds, Slow Dragon, Lawrence Marrero, Elton Purnell, all came later.

ctx.x: Louis started making high notes after Kid Reno. He was inspired by Reno. Kid Reno was, he never left New Orleans. He was just, he was happy with New Orleans, you know what I mean? But in the 20s, Kid Reno was playing plenty of horn, man. He was really blowing.

Could we talk a little bit about the rhythm sections in those days? Yeah. You said that the Bunk band in 44 was a hark back to the old style prior to 1920 because Bunk hadn't played for those years. Yeah. Would you say that the rhythm section, that was Baby Dodds, Slow Dragon, Lawrence Marrero, Elton Purnell, all came later. Would you say that that rhythm section was similar to the ones before 1920?

I will say it, yes. You know, they had the original beat. I'll be truthful with you. I didn't hear any bad rhythm sections from New Orleans. Even now, I don't think they have this thing, it's a natural. They get to our bass and drums and things, they play together. They play for the other guys. They didn't do a lot of solo work, but they played together. It was a beautiful thing. They didn't blast or nothing in those days, you know. It was full. We didn't need a piano. No.
